statement: Khaybar was a fortified oasis rich in date palms, some days' journey north of Madinah.
Leaders at Khaybar had incited the Confederates; he marched on Khaybar at the start of year 7, after Hudaybiyyah.
alternatives: Muharram of year 7 by most reports; some say the end of year 6.

statement: Salamah ibn al-Akwa: on the night march Amir recited verses beginning 'O Allah, had it not been for You we would not have been guided'.
Anas: they prayed Fajr near Khaybar in the dark and rode in; the people coming out to work cried 'Muhammad and the army'.
notes: Machine-checked. The spades and baskets are in parallel narrations (Bukhari 2945), from memory.

statement: The forts held out for some days.

Sahl ibn Sa'd: 'Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger...'; the people's hopes; Ali's eyes healed after he prayed for him; Ali's question and the reply: advance steadily, invite them to Islam; that Allah guide one man through you is better than red camels.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for the first half; Ali's question and the reply are in the remainder of the same narrations, from memory. The narration says he applied his saliva to Ali's eyes and prayed for him; the script says 'prayed for him'.

statement: Ibn Umar: he left the people of Khaybar on the land to cultivate it for half of its produce.
Anas: Safiyyah bint Huyayy was among the captives; he freed her and married her.
notes: In the remainder of Bukhari 371, from memory.

statement: A Jewish woman brought him a poisoned sheep; he ate some; asked 'shall we not kill her?', he said no.
notes: Number from memory; not machine-checked. Other reports say she was later executed in retaliation when a Companion who had eaten died; not narrated. Reviewer to decide.

statement: Abu Musa: his party from Yemen was carried by ship to the Negus, stayed with Ja'far, and all came to the Prophet at the conquest of Khaybar; some said 'we emigrated before you'; Asma bint Umays reported it; he said the people of the ship have two emigrations.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for the first part; the Prophet's reply is in the remainder of 4230, from memory (the remark was made by Umar to Asma).
